summary: A person or tenant, as a picture, initials or a generic mark.

pairs.dont: Render an avatar with only an image source.
pairs.do: Always give it initials or the generic person to fall back to.
pairs.why: Profile pictures 404 more than anything else on a page. Without a fallback the layout collapses to an empty circle.

pairs.dont: Let the dot be the only thing saying someone is offline.
pairs.do: Give AvatarStatus a label, and repeat the state in text nearby.
pairs.why: A colour on a 10px dot is invisible to a screen reader and hard for anyone who does not know the convention.

pairs.dont: Hang the only route to a profile off clicking the avatar.
pairs.do: Wrap it in a real link or button with a name.
pairs.why: An avatar is an image. Nothing about it says it can be activated, and nothing announces where it goes.

pairs.dont: Use initials alone in a list people scan to find someone.
pairs.do: Put the name beside it; keep the avatar as recognition, not identification.
pairs.why: Two colleagues share initials more often than you would think, and initials do not disambiguate them.

pairs.dont: Mix avatar sizes down one list.
pairs.do: Pick the size from the row it sits in — xs in dense tables, md in headers.
pairs.why: The avatar sets the row's optical height. Changing it mid-list makes the whole list look misaligned.

pairs.dont: Stack twenty avatars because twenty people are on the incident.
pairs.do: Cap with max and let the +N carry the rest.
pairs.why: Past about five, the faces stop identifying anyone and the row just eats width.

a11y: AvatarStatus carries role="img" with an aria-label — "online", "3 unread", or whatever label says. A dot that silently turns green tells a screen reader nothing.
The User fallback icon and the verified badge are both aria-hidden; the status wrapper's label is the only text in it.
The overflow "+N" button takes an explicit label. It is an icon and a number with no sentence of its own.
